extracted.intended_audience: mid-career academic researchers (recently tenured or tenure-equivalent) and institutional nominators/administrators in STEM fields
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and selection criteria for nominations and invited applications to the Schmidt Science Polymaths program, which funds mid-career researchers pursuing substantive disciplinary or methodological shifts. Covers eligibility, nomination process, application contents, review expectations, award terms, and reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenure/t​enure-equivalent timing eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Have achieved tenure or equivalent status within the past three calendar years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three-year window is intended to reflect a period of a candidate’s career, not necessarily their position. Eligible candidates should have received tenure or a permanent faculty position for the first time at any institution within the past three years. Candidates tenured more than three years ago at one institution who have recently been granted tenure at a new institution are not eligible. Candidates with multiple tenured appointments are eligible only if all tenured appointments were granted within the last three calendar years. The program recognizes that tenure systems vary and will work with institutions to determine suitable tenure equivalencies; contact the program for special cases. The eligibility window may consider exceptions (e.g., family or medical leave) with appropriate justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of accomplishment in STEM fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a remarkable record of accomplishment in mathematics, computer science, natural sciences, and/or engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a core qualification — reviewers seek exceptional academic researchers with demonstrated achievements in these fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated interdisciplinarity / polymathic track record
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a demonstrated history of pursuing and publishing results in more than one field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program targets researchers who already exhibit capacity to work across multiple research topics/problems; interdisciplinarity is a positive selection factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for funding to enable new directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate a need for additional funding to enable new experiments, explorations, or shifts in research directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should justify how award funds would make possible exploration of new ideas, risky theories, or substantive disciplinary/methodological shifts that likely would not otherwise receive support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field competitiveness considerations (medical/social sciences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who work solely in a clinical setting or within particular areas of medical sciences, or who work primarily in the social sciences, are not as competitive as candidates who exhibit track records and capacity to work across a broader set of research topics and problems in the sciences and/or engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a competitiveness note rather than an absolute ineligibility; it signals reviewer preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation-only application / nomination sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to Schmidt Science Polymaths are by invitation only; nominations come from a select group of leading science, technology, and engineering institutions and a broader call for nominations from targeted leaders within Schmidt Sciences and the scientific communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all nominees will be invited to apply — the Polymath Team first checks eligibility (tenure/equivalent and research areas) before inviting eligible nominees to submit an application. Candidates cannot self-nominate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional nominating partner requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions wishing to become nominating partners must submit an interest form with details on the institution’s tenure or equivalent policy and information on the institution’s fitness for the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program periodically evaluates and updates its list of nominating partners; interested institutions should contact the provided email for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials required if invited
rubrics_metrics.description: Invited applications will include a CV, information about past accomplishments, a description of potential problems or projects the candidate might pursue if awarded, and a list of references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application is intended as a space to showcase potential new research directions and creativity; awardees are not bound to pursue the exact projects proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: References: substance and whom to choose
rubrics_metrics.description: References should know you or your work well enough to testify not just to your accomplishments, but also your creativity, adventurousness, and the likelihood you will pursue excellent new directions in research given flexible resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References may include past advisors and/or collaborators and should be able to speak to the applicant’s readiness to pursue ambitious, cross-disciplinary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: No self-nomination
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations must come from eligible nominating partners or targeted leaders; contact the program if your institution’s eligibility is unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-application rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates may be nominated and apply more than once but only during the tenure eligibility window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-applicants are strongly encouraged to revisit and revise their application; do not submit the exact same materials. The program does not provide specific candidate feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline for nominations/applications/decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations are typically collected from June to mid-August, applications are due in October, and decisions are shared in April.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these windows for planning nominations and application preparation; contact the program for any deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget not required / award flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: You do not need to include a budget as part of your application for your proposed projects/problems; Polymath awardees are not bound to pursue the projects proposed in their applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application emphasizes ideas and direction rather than detailed project budgets; however, awardees should be prepared to report on expenditures annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count and citation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations do not count toward the word limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations/references are excluded from the word count; check application instructions for specific word limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures in application
rubrics_metrics.description: You may include up to two figures in your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program recommends limiting figures/schematics and using them only when they significantly enhance a reviewer’s understanding of your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and review standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are reviewed by a team of experts; the review is highly selective with fewer than 10% of applicants selected each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are evaluating exceptional promise for adventurous, cross-disciplinary research and likelihood of high-impact breakthroughs enabled by flexible funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and intended use
rubrics_metrics.description: Each professor will be awarded $500,000 per year, paid through their institution, for up to five years to help support a research group through talent, such as three to four students or postdocs, and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants are intended to enable exploration of new ideas across disciplines and to test risky theories that may not otherwise receive funding; they are not intended to relieve the researcher of pursuing other grants nor to be large enough to fully support a modern lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and engagement requirements for awardees
rubrics_metrics.description: Polymaths are expected to complete a report each year for the duration of their time as Awardees; reports include financial accounting of funds spent, a narrative report detailing successes, failures, and future plans, a list of outputs, and other information about Polymath-funded work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to the annual report, awardees are expected to meet with the Polymath team virtually approximately once per quarter, are invited to attend an in-person convening 1-2 times per year, and will have a mid-term and a final review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Schmidt Science Polymath Award is expected to be processed as a grant to a university to provide general support for an awardee’s research; as a result, the program anticipates that no indirect costs will be taken from the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting is expected to come directly from the grantee with minimal (if any) assistance from the university.
